deviations.description: /please grammar for the 5 destructive action classes
deviations.reason: The plan names the 5 action classes to add but does not specify the exact /please free-text grammar for them (only the push grammar is spelled out in detail). Designed a literal-git-command-shaped grammar ('git reset --hard', 'git clean -fd', 'git checkout -- <path>', 'git restore <path>', 'git stash drop'/'clear', 'git checkout -f'/'git switch -f') since it mirrors what a user would naturally type and requires no new vocabulary to learn. REMOTE/REF/FORCE use fixed sentinels (REMOTE=local, REF=current branch or HEAD if detached, FORCE=0) since these actions have no remote/force concept, matching the sentinels guard-destructive-git.sh's own grant check consumes.
deviations.annotation: *(deviation: altered — literal-git-command-shaped /please grammar for the 5 destructive classes, with fixed REMOTE=local/FORCE=0 sentinels; see hooks/please-grant.sh comments)*

verification_notes: test-guard-destructive-git.sh: 72/72 pass unmodified both before and after the edit (pure-addition witness). Ad-hoc fixture verification: (1) /please git reset --hard mints a reset_hard grant; (2) a dirty-tree git reset --hard with that grant present is ALLOWED and the grant is consumed (file gone); (3) a second attempt with no grant is BLOCKED with the original message; (4) git add -A with a live reset_hard grant present is STILL BLOCKED (over-staging immunity preserved, grant untouched since over-staging's exit 2 happens strictly before the grant-check code is ever reached); (5) the history-rewrite predicate still fires (git commit --amend under a live lock, BLOCKED) with an unrelated reset_hard grant present and live, grant left untouched.
